claim: Top and base beams (2 x UPN 160, S275) stay below yield at 294 kN
law: Beam bending; S275 yield 275 MPa (EN 10025-2)

claim: 60 mm 42CrMo4 load pin carries 294 kN in bending without yield
law: Pin in double shear and bending; 42CrMo4 quenched and tempered yield about 650 MPa

claim: M16 10.9 joint bolts carry their share of 294 kN in double shear
law: Bolt shear resistance 0.5 x fub / gamma_M2 = 0.5 x 1000 / 1.25 = 400 MPa (EN 1993-1-8)

claim: Deflection between the molds below 1 mm at the 10 t structural check case
law: Beam and column elastic deflection, E = 200 GPa

claim: The bolted upright joints do not slip in their 18 mm holes at 294 kN (preloaded M16 10.9)
law: Slip resistance n mu Fp,C with Fp,C = 0.7 fub As (EN 1993-1-8 category C practice); slip factor 0.2 for unprepared surfaces
check: 36.7749 kN per bolt <= 43.96 kN per bolt
closed_by: PPR-BLD-001 step 8 (preload torque); PPR-CAL-001 v0.12 section 4

claim: A pot filter can be formed within the 5.4 t working force limit
law: A low-cost press forms round-bottom pot filters with a 2 t jack (Henry, Maley and Mehta 2013); factories press flat-bottomed 280 mm pots on 20 t jack presses without a published working force. The pressed pot here is about 18 % larger than the factory form, so the force it needs is found in trials (decided 2026-10-02); 10 t is a structural check case, not a working force (D9, decided by Amish 2026-10-25)
closed_by: Pressing trials with a partner factory, starting near 2 t (decided 2026-10-02); working force limit 5.4 t (D9, decided by Amish 2026-10-25)

claim: Mean pressure on the clay at 10 t is about 0.9 MPa
law: Pressure = force / projected area

claim: One operator can pump each pressing by hand (power, at 10 t with 85 % jack efficiency)
law: Work = force x distance: the load builds over the last 20 mm (half of 10 t on average) after a 90 mm approach at 0.5 t, about 1 min of pumping, 85 % pump and seal efficiency; sustained human output about 75 W

claim: Pump handle force stays within repetitive-work guidance at the working force limit of 5.4 t
law: Handle force = jack force x piston-to-ram area ratio / lever ratio / efficiency: about 126 N at 5.4 t frictionless and about 148 N with 85 % pump and seal efficiency, inside the 150 N screening limit (the earlier 6.4 t limit gave about 175 N with efficiency); about 70 strokes a pressing at about 50 a minute; EN 1005-3 frequency and duration multipliers not yet applied
check: 126 N frictionless, 148 N at 85 % efficiency, against a 150 N screen; working force limit lowered from 6.4 to 5.4 t (D9, decided by Amish 2026-10-25)
closed_by: To confirm: EN 1005-3 assessment with the bought jack's piston, lever and efficiency data (PPR-CAL-001, next session); the two-speed pump (D6) stays open if trials need more than 5.4 t

claim: Pin, beams and cast molds survive 20,000 pressings a year at 10 t
law: Fatigue: beam welded detail category 71 MPa at 2 million cycles (EN 1993-1-9); 42CrMo4 endurance about 400 MPa; cast Al-Si about 50 MPa
closed_by: This file (stress at 10 t is one third of the 294 kN value)

claim: Reference filter holds 12.30 L to the brim
law: Frustum volume

claim: 69 pots per 6 h at a 5.2 min cycle
law: Rate = time / cycle

claim: 0.1 L reads as 1.69 mm on the T-gauge
law: Volume = area x height (water surface about 275 mm across)
check: claimed 0.0591716 m2 of water surface, estimate 0.0594 m2 of water surface (ratio 1.00)

claim: Charge of 9.59 kg of mix per pot
law: Factory practice 8 to 9.5 kg per filter (Rayner 2009)

claim: A push of about 850 N at 1 m tips the unanchored press (centre of mass 246 mm behind the front foot edge, carriage out)
law: Restoring moment = weight x lever arm
check: claimed 850 N m, estimate 849 N m (ratio 1.00)

claim: Fired pot of 4.88 kg from an 8.72 kg pressed pot
law: Mass balance: water leaves, clay loses about 10 % on ignition, rice husk leaves 15 to 20 % silica ash (ash now in CAL)

claim: Rice husk or sawdust burns out on firing and leaves the pores that set flow
law: Combustion of cellulose well below the 800 to 900 C firing; pore size set by burnout particle size (Heijman et al. 2015)
check: PotPress controls wall thickness only; recipe and firing out of scope

claim: Aluminum mold faces and polyethylene liners do not contaminate the pot
law: Aluminium worn off by wet clay oxidises to alumina, already a clay constituent; the real risk is lead, cadmium, copper or zinc in scrap alloy, and wheel scrap carries lead balance weights and brass valve stems
check: A356 wheel scrap only, sorted before melting (weights, valve stems, steel and paint removed); a chill sample of each melt checked by spark OES, or handheld XRF for lead, before pouring; lead and cadmium within the EN 601 limits (values to confirm); recorded per heat (PR-012 verification)

claim: Silver treatment is outside PotPress; a silver-treated filter can stay under WHO's 0.1 mg/L reference value
law: WHO silver chemical fact sheet (2022): provisional reference value 0.1 mg/L, no health-based guideline value
check: No claim made by PotPress; noted for the factory

claim: Flow changes about 2.3 % per C near 25 C
law: Darcy flow scales with 1/viscosity of water
check: claimed 2.3 % per C, estimate 2.33 % per C (ratio 0.99)

claim: PotPress makes no pathogen-removal claim; locally made pot filters cut E. coli by about 99 %
law: Brown and Sobsey 2010; WHO HWT scheme 2-star target is 2 log for bacteria
check: The press makes consistent pots; removal must be lab-tested per batch (stated in PRC Safety)

claim: Parts over 25 kg (female mold 39.6 kg, platen 39.6 kg, top crossbeam 38.0 kg, base beam 34.2 kg, male mold 26.3 kg) are lifted safely
law: Team lifting: two people carry about two thirds of their combined capacity (about 31 kg at 23 kg each), lower still at 1.5 m height and for bulky loads. M12 eye bolt in steel plate or 26 mm of Al-Si thread: tens of kN to strip against about 0.2 kN per leg
check: Every part over 25 kg goes on a 0.5 t chain block: female mold by two M12 DIN 580 eye bolts in its steel base plate, male mold by two in its flange top, both on a two-leg sling with shackles and the eyes shimmed into the sling plane; beams and platen in a round sling. Eye bolts out and holes plugged before pressing. The 40 kg limit in PR-008 is a transport limit

claim: Silica-bearing clay dust (and rice husk ash in fired trimmings) is a respiratory hazard controlled by wet work and P2 or N95 masks
law: Crystalline silica causes silicosis; wet methods and respirators are standard controls; air monitoring shows whether they work

claim: Zinc fume from welding galvanised mesh is controlled by grinding the coating off and ventilation
law: Zinc oxide fume causes metal fume fever
check: Stated in the build plan safety notes

claim: The fired filter comes out at the 280 mm reference size
law: Clay shrinks on drying and firing, typically 6 to 10 % linear for earthenware filter mixes; the mold cavity is the fired size divided by (1 - shrinkage). CMWG 2011 notes grog changing fired size enough that pots no longer fit receptacles
check: claimed 280 mm inner rim, estimate 280 mm inner rim (ratio 1.00)
closed_by: PPR-DDR-006 (D2): cavity scaled for 8 % total shrinkage (CLAY_SHRINK in cad/src/model.py), to be replaced by the partner clay's test-bar value (ASTM C326 method) before patterns are printed

claim: The mix fills the cavity, air escapes and the green pot releases and survives the demold tilt
law: Plastic clay pressing between two-part molds is established practice in over 50 factories; vents and liners are standard
check: Within known science; mold vents and release confirmed in the first pressing trials (BLD first checks)

claim: Casting patterns print on a printer with a true 250 x 250 mm bed
law: 486 mm pattern split into quadrants; a 250 x 210 mm or 220 x 220 mm bed does not fit

claim: Hand lapping to printed templates reaches +/-0.3 mm on a 400 mm casting
law: Grinding and filing to templates reach +/-0.3 mm in toolroom practice; printed PLA templates can be off by 0.2 to 0.5 % over 400 mm, which the tolerance budget does not yet include
check: Within known science; practical risk carried in RSK and requirement PR-002 (at risk)

claim: Guard openings meet ISO 13857 Table 4 for their distance from moving parts
law: ISO 13857:2019 Table 4
check: 23 openings checked from the model; Table 7 (lower limbs) and the floor gap not yet checked; signature by a competent person is a hold point

claim: Option B: the toggle gives about 1.4 t at 0.35 mm from straight (0.16 t at 30 mm, 7 t at 0.014 mm)
law: Virtual work on the toggle with the lever rigid on the upper link: F = T / (2 L sin theta); the kit 1.8 estimate (2 t at 0.35 mm) was about 40 % high
closed_by: PPR-OPT-001 v0.3 (figures restated from the detailed model)

claim: Option B: the 80 x 40 mm lower link does not buckle at 1.5 times 10 t
law: Euler buckling of a pinned strut, P = pi^2 E I / L^2, E = 200 GPa
closed_by: This file (model link 80 x 40 x 400 mm)

claim: Option B: the 40 mm clevis pins carry 1.5 times 10 t in double shear
law: Pin shear 0.5 x fub / gamma_M2 with fub 600 MPa (EN 1993-1-8 pin practice)
closed_by: This file (model pins 40 mm, ISO 2341 B)

claim: Option B: the 40 mm clevis pins stay below yield in bending at 1.5 times 10 t
law: Pin bending M = F/2 (a/2 + g + b/4), sigma = M / (pi d^3 / 32), yield about 640 MPa (8.8 class pin steel); the 30 mm pins first drawn reached about 510 MPa
closed_by: cad/src/options_bc.py (pins 30 to 40 mm after the independent review, 2026-10-24)

claim: Option C: two people at 300 N on the 450 mm capstan give about 6.7 t with the thrust ball bearing (3.6 t with a plain collar)
law: Power screw torque T = F (dm / 2) tan(lambda + phi) plus collar friction; the detailed model's thrust ball bearing cuts the collar term, giving about 6.7 t
closed_by: PPR-OPT-001 v0.3 (thrust bearing in the detailed model)

claim: Option C: the Tr40 x 7 screw self-locks (lead angle below the friction angle)
law: Self-locking when lambda < phi

claim: Option C: the screw does not buckle at 1.5 times 10 t over its free length of about 0.4 m closed (0.7 m open)
law: Euler buckling, pinned at the nut and the thrust swivel, P = pi^2 E I / L^2 on the root diameter, at the open length as the worst case
closed_by: This file (model: 330 mm swivel to crown closed, plus the 310 mm opening)

claim: Option C: about 43 turns cover the 300 mm opening
law: Turns = travel / lead
